clue.text: Cover for the present?

parts.note: read 'present' not as the current time but as a gift, and the cover is the decorated sheet folded round it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what will stand in for things right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' tempts as 'the here and now'; the question mark tells you it is the gift, and the cover is what it is wrapped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative sheets used to enclose birthday or Christmas gifts go by this name.

clue.text: Long rows of bloomers?

parts.note: 'rows' rhymes with 'cows' here, meaning quarrels, and the 'bloomers' are flowers: the white and red emblems of York and Lancaster

explanation.surface: A gardener admires lengthy lines of flowering plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like lines of plants, but read it as fights; the drawn-out fifteenth-century English civil conflict between York and Lancaster took its name from each house's flower badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The houses of York and Lancaster, badged with white and red flowers, fought a long series of dynastic battles in fifteenth-century England.

clue.text: A dreary opening last month -— suitable for mature persons only

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of dreary is used

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, is the old business abbreviation for 'of last month'

explanation.surface: A gloomy start to the previous month, with a warning that it is only for grown-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) appears in old commercial letters: 'your letter of the 5th ult.' means the 5th of last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Films or books labelled this way are restricted to grown-up audiences.

clue.text: Like operation carried out on foot — producing a red instep

definitions.text: Like operation carried out on foot

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are worked up into something new, as a show is produced from raw material

explanation.surface: Foot surgery has left a patient with a reddened arch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests surgery on the foot; the definition means done by walking. 'Producing' rearranges A RED INSTEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes travel or activity done by walking rather than riding.

clue.text: Care for track where two-year-olds run

definitions.text: Care for track where two-year-olds run

parts.words: Care for track where two-year-olds run
parts.note: two-year-olds are both toddlers in day care and young racehorses, which run in a race reserved for horses of that age

explanation.surface: Someone wants a running track minded for very young children.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing a race restricted to two-year-old horses bears the same name as a place where toddlers are looked after.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a place where small children are minded and a flat race for juvenile horses.

clue.text: Reservation issue?

parts.note: 'issue' means offspring and the 'reservation' is land set aside for Native Americans, so this is a baby there

explanation.surface: A complaint about a booking at a hotel or restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like a booking and 'issue' like a problem; read them as Native American land and offspring. The word, taken from an Algonquian language, names a baby, and also the carrier for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from an Algonquian language and means a young child among Native Americans.

clue.text: European repellent to his own kind

definitions.meaning: an end of a magnet pushes away a like magnetic end

explanation.surface: A continental is said to be unpleasant to his compatriots.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on magnetism: like magnetic ends push each other away, so this one is 'repellent' to its own kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Poland is a European, and a magnet's north or south end repels another of the same type.

clue.text: Aggregate on the way?

parts.note: 'aggregate' is crushed stone rather than a total, and 'the way' is a road it is laid on

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a running total is still coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way' suggests something coming; it means literally on the road. 'Aggregate' is the builders' word for broken stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone used to make or repair road surfaces is known by this term.

clue.text: Broadcasting stinks — I had crime story thrown out!

indicators.note: something thrown out is disordered, so the letters of these words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A complainant says radio output is dreadful and their crime drama was rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinks' is old British school slang for chemistry, so 'broadcasting stinks' is radio (broadcasting) plus chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry of radioactive substances, with 'broadcasting' standing for radio and 'stinks' schoolboy slang for chemistry.

clue.text: It's a cycle journey there and back

definitions.meaning: a cycle comes full circle back to where it started
an outward trip followed by a return

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a bike ride is an out-and-back excursion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' looks like a bicycle but means a complete circuit; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A circuit that returns to its starting point, and a return excursion, share this name.

clue.text: Climber uses a metal spike to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the words a and metal spike are read backwards as one run

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike hammered into wood

explanation.surface: A mountaineer relies on a piton to get back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a plant. 'To return' turns A NAIL around.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees.

clue.text: Captain put out to sea at 6

definitions.note: Captain Lawrence Oates of Scott's Antarctic expedition

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's master set sail at six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At 6' sends you to 6 down, POLE: Captain Oates walked out into the blizzard on the return from the South Pole. 'Put out' rearranges TO SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Oates, an army captain, famously left the tent on Scott's ill-fated polar journey.

clue.text: Head of English attending fashion-school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of English is taken

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: A senior English teacher joins a fashion college.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'fashion-school' is only for the surface; split it. TON is a dated word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known English public school at Windsor, beside the Thames.

clue.text: Body of Bantu warriors, some limping

indicators.note: some of the word limping, a run of letters inside it, is what is wanted

explanation.surface: Several soldiers in an African troop are hobbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from inside LIMPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment or army of Zulu fighters, a Bantu people of southern Africa.

clue.text: Working like a charm for Scott

definitions.text: Working like a charm for Scott

parts.words: Working like a charm for Scott
parts.note: 'working like a charm' usually means going smoothly; here it means acting as a magic charm, and Sir Walter Scott wrote a novel named after such an amulet

explanation.surface: Things went perfectly for someone called Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: After 11 across, 'Scott' suggests the polar explorer; it is Sir Walter Scott, whose crusader novel is called 'The Talisman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means having the magic power of an amulet, the subject of a Walter Scott novel.

clue.text: The impulse to change end comes from divine intervention

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for impulse is swapped for another

parts.note: an urge is a sudden impulse

explanation.surface: Someone's urge to alter the ending was inspired from on high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To change end' replaces the final E of URGE; the clue does not say what with, so the Y comes from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The working of miracles or magic through the agency of gods or spirits.

clue.text: England's opening pair hit back and run across

parts.note: the opening pair of letters of the word England
to counter is to hit back at an attack

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen strike back and dash for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where the opening pair are the first two batsmen; here it is the first two letters of ENGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To run across someone is to meet them by chance.

clue.text: Bouncy sort of band

definitions.meaning: springy, returning to shape after stretching
a stretchy rubber loop used to hold things together

explanation.surface: A lively kind of music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians; it is a rubber band.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy material returns to shape, and a rubber loop for bundling things carries the same adjective.

clue.text: Delight in song from France

parts.note: en is French for 'in', as 'from France' tells you
a chant is a simple song or melody

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in a French tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From France' asks for the French word for 'in', EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate someone is to fill them with pleasure.

clue.text: Squally in borders of the Trossachs — low pressure areas

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other here, the stormy word set within the borders
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: squally weather is rough and stormy

explanation.surface: Stormy weather on the edges of a Scottish beauty spot brings depressions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trossachs are a wooded Highland area in Scotland; its first and last letters are T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology these are elongated regions of reduced atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Scots give Ben, in the interior, help in the field

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another, in the interior of the Scots word

parts.note: gie is the Scots form of give
ben is the Scots word for a mountain or hill

explanation.surface: Scottish people send help to a man named Ben in remote country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' looks like a man's name; it is a Scottish mountain. 'In the interior' puts HILL inside GIE. 'In the field' means out hunting or fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish attendant who assists a sportsman when shooting or fishing.

clue.text: Gallery to close? What a blessing!

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A relieved visitor hears the art gallery is shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallery' suggests an art museum; it is the top balcony of a theatre, called 'the gods'. 'What a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome that arrives just when needed is a boon from heaven.

clue.text: No teachers available for duty

definitions.meaning: with no teachers around, the job falls to us pupils: it is the answer

explanation.surface: Staff shortages mean nobody can take playground supervision.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical reading: if no teachers are available, the job is 'on us'. Run those two words together for a word meaning a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or obligation that someone must bear.

clue.text: Certificate of repayment expressed as a decimal in the books

definitions.meaning: a debt certificate promising repayment with interest

definitions.text: expressed as a decimal in the books
definitions.meaning: Ian Fleming's spy is agent 007, a number that looks like a decimal fraction

explanation.surface: A loan document shows a figure written as a decimal in the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The books' look like accounts; they are Ian Fleming's novels, whose hero is codenamed 007, written like a decimal.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt security promising repayment, and Fleming's secret agent known by the number 007.

clue.text: La Boheme set around a resort in America

indicators.note: one piece is set around another, enclosing it

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: An opera production is staged near an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'La Boheme' stands for its heroine, MIMI, who is 'set around' A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Florida city famous for beaches and tourism.

clue.text: A true: definition of a region

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry gives an accurate meaning for an area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definition' signals that the closing words are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to an area or district.

clue.text: In favour of a boat that has an outrigger

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone supports a vessel fitted with a side float.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast Malay or Pacific sailing craft with a single outrigger.

clue.text: Unusual trees in compound

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of trees appear in a different order

explanation.surface: Odd trees grow within an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like an enclosure; it is a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic chemical formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Judo pupil doing well in open land round city

definitions.meaning: a judo student who has reached a middle grade wears a belt of this colour
protected countryside around a town where building is restricted

explanation.surface: A promising martial arts student lives on the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Judo grades are marked by belt colours; in Britain the same phrase names protected countryside ringing a town where building is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured judo grade, and a planning zone of undeveloped countryside around a British town.

clue.text: Perhaps play as child, or as Gershwin played?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the following letters might be put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to play like a youngster or like the great composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges PLAY AS CHILD OR. Gershwin wrote 'Rhapsody in Blue', so playing as he did is playing in the manner of a rhapsody.
explanation.definitionFit: In an ecstatic, free-flowing manner, like the composer's famous blue rhapsody.
